correctness.rationale: All assumptions and quantifiers are explicit. The four-leaf PGF identity is reconstructed from its 16 survivor subsets in each shape; the graft recursion cancels equal all-extinct contributions and proves the all-n polynomial identity. Differentiation at z=1 gives the strict expectation advantage. Taking the sum of coefficients above the natural half-total cutoff yields the exact threshold sign; all rooted binary shapes with at most four leaves are exhausted (one at n=2, one at n=3, two at n=4). The standalone standard-library checker independently verified exact polynomial coefficients for n=4 through 11. No finite check is presented as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The primary 2008 distribution paper explicitly asks how maximizing expected PD relates to minimizing a critical-loss tail; this theorem gives a rigorous sharp answer for the natural half-initial-PD retention target. Five taxa are minimal, and the exact crossover q=(n−4)/(n−2) holds for every n, monotonically approaching 1. A strategy/tree with uniformly higher expected retained history can have lower probability of meeting a fixed retention goal over a nonempty extinction-risk interval, a substantive risk-sensitive distinction rather than an arbitrary computed coefficient. This is not claimed to predict real-world extinction outcomes.
